[S2] There was a strong association between mandibular torus and presence of both bruxism and wear facets.

[S4] The present study demonstrated that provisional implant-supported prostheses are capable of restoring the EMG activity immediately after prostheses fixation and that they do not require an adaptation period.
[S5] It is suggested that bruxism may be associated with an increased risk of dental implant failure.
[S6] This should be considered in treatment planning and management of implant patients.
[S7] However, the relationship between bruxism and implant complications remains complex, requiring standardized diagnostic criteria and evidence-based treatment protocols.

[S9] In otherwise healthy individuals, bruxism should not be consid- ered as a disorder, but rather as a behaviour that can be a risk (and/or protective) factor for certain clinical consequences.
